---
title: "Seeded batch sampling"
---

Every supported distribution has a `dist_{family}_rng()` function that returns
ordinary PHP numeric arrays. Sampling uses mature Rust RNG libraries already in
the dependency graph: pinned `rand 0.9.5` and `rand_chacha 0.9.0`, now explicit
stats-core dependencies. No package versions were upgraded. Each call owns and
restarts its own ChaCha20 state from the supplied seed.

## API and state ownership

The signature is `dist_{family}_rng(int $n, int $seed, ...distribution parameters): array`.
The family parameters and defaults are exactly those of the corresponding
[probability API](distributions.qmd#families-and-parameterizations).

```php
$normal = Phit\dist_normal_rng(n: 5, seed: 42); // Default mean 0, SD 1.
$measurements = Phit\dist_normal_rng(n: 8, seed: 20261012, mean: 10, sd: .5);
$counts = Phit\dist_poisson_rng(n: 8, seed: 20261013, lambda: 3.2);
$beta = Phit\dist_beta_rng(n: 8, seed: 17, alpha: 2, beta: 5);
```

| Function | Parameters after n and seed |
| --- | --- |
| `dist_normal_rng` | mean = 0, sd = 1 |
| `dist_t_rng` | df |
| `dist_chisquare_rng` | df |
| `dist_f_rng` | df1, df2 |
| `dist_beta_rng` | alpha, beta |
| `dist_gamma_rng` | shape, scale = 1 |
| `dist_exponential_rng` | rate = 1 |
| `dist_lognormal_rng` | meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1 |
| `dist_logistic_rng` | location = 0, scale = 1 |
| `dist_binomial_rng` | size, prob |
| `dist_poisson_rng` | lambda |
| `dist_nbinom_rng` | size, prob |
| `dist_nbinom_mu_rng` | size, mu |

`n` is an integer in `[0,1000000]`; `seed` is a nonnegative PHP integer, including
zero, up to PHP_INT_MAX (2^63−1 on the supported 64-bit platforms). Both arguments
are required. Every successful result is a packed `list<float>` of exactly n
finite values; discrete counts are also floats. There is no scalar sampling form
or additional `_array` suffix because sampling is already a batch operation.

The same seed and parameters reproduce exactly the same result within the same
build. Asking for fewer samples returns the prefix of a longer call. Calls for
other families or seeds do not advance a shared stream. PHP's `mt_srand()` and
application RNG state are not read or changed.

Because a seed selects the same underlying uniform sequence across families,
reusing it deliberately couples results through their quantiles. Use distinct
seeds for separate batches when independent streams are intended. There is no
implicit time-based seed, OS entropy lookup, retained RNG object or hidden global
state. The runnable `examples/rng.php` verifies repeatability and prefix behavior.

## Uniform, categorical and permutation sampling

Four samplers have no probability API. They take the same `n` and `seed`
arguments, have the same limits, and consume one uniform from the same stream
per draw.

| Function | R equivalent | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dist_uniform_rng(n, seed, min = 0, max = 1)` | `runif(n, min, max)` | `list<float>` |
| `dist_categorical_rng(n, seed, prob)` | `sample(length(prob), n, replace = TRUE, prob = prob) - 1` | `list<int>` |
| `dist_categorical_rows_rng(seed, prob)` | one `sample(K, 1, prob = prob[i, ]) - 1` per row | `list<int>` |
| `permutation_rng(n, seed, size = null)` | `sample(n, size) - 1` | `list<int>` |

```php
$x = Phit\dist_uniform_rng(n: 5, seed: 1, min: -1, max: 1);
$categories = ['returns', 'sizing', 'quality'];
$picked = array_map(fn ($k) => $categories[$k],
    Phit\dist_categorical_rng(n: 5, seed: 2, prob: [.2, .5, .3]));
// One rating per review, each from its own probabilities.
$ratings = Phit\dist_categorical_rows_rng(seed: 3, prob: [[.1, .6, .3], [.7, .2, .1]]);
$shuffled = Phit\permutation_rng(n: 10, seed: 4); // All of 0..9.
$subset = Phit\permutation_rng(n: 10, seed: 4, size: 3); // Its first three.
```

Indices are 0-based positions, so they index PHP lists directly. Add one for
R's 1-based categories.

- **Uniform.** Each draw is `min + (max - min) * u`, as in R's `runif()`. `min`
  must not exceed `max`, and `min == max` gives `min`.
- **Categorical.** `prob` is a list of finite, nonnegative weights with a
  positive sum. As in R's `sample()`, the weights are divided by their sum. The
  draw for `u` is the first index `k` with `u * sum(prob) < prob[0] + ... +
  prob[k]`. A zero weight is never drawn. If rounding puts `u * sum(prob)` at or
  above the sum, the last positive weight is drawn.
- **Rows.** `dist_categorical_rows_rng()` takes a list of up to one million
  such vectors and returns one draw per row. Rows may have different lengths.
  Draw `i` uses the `i`th uniform, so a list of equal rows gives
  `dist_categorical_rng()`'s result for the same seed.
- **Permutation.** `permutation_rng()` runs a partial Fisher–Yates shuffle of
  `0..n-1`. Step `i` swaps position `i` with `i + floor(u * (n - i))`, capped at
  `n - 1`. `size` is in `[0, n]` and defaults to `n`. A smaller `size` returns
  the prefix of the full permutation.

These samplers use the same ChaCha20 uniforms as the other families. Their
results therefore differ from R's for the same seed, as the other families'
results do. A non-list `prob`, a negative weight, a zero sum, `min > max`, or
`size > n` raises 1001. A nonfinite weight, weight sum, bound, or uniform draw
raises 1003. More than one million draws or rows, or `n` above one million for
a permutation, raises 1007.

## Numerical method and reproducibility

For every output, ChaCha20 provides a 64-bit word; rand's `Open01<f64>` maps its
upper 52 bits to a midpoint strictly inside `(0,1)`. The value is transformed by
the existing validated inverse CDF. The algorithm consumes one uniform per sample,
including point masses. This uses the established numerical quantile kernels for
all 13 parameterizations, without introducing a separate distribution backend.

The open interval excludes infinite support endpoints. The finite uniform grid
also limits represented tail probabilities: its minimum is 2^-53 and its maximum
is 1−2^-53. This implementation favors a small, consistent numerical path over
distribution-specific rejection samplers; [benchmarks](benchmarks/rng.qmd) record
the cost for normal, beta and Poisson batches.

The pinned rand_core `seed_from_u64` expands the integer with its documented PCG32
mapping into the 256-bit ChaCha key. Exact uniform vectors are checked independently
in Python. Dependency or quantile-algorithm changes can change seeded samples and
must be reviewed as reproducibility changes. Bitwise transformed-sample agreement
across different library versions, compilers or platform math libraries is not
promised; seeds are not claimed to match R or NumPy's unrelated default engines.
The full dependency lock and algorithm are recorded for reproducible runs.

## Validation

Distribution parameter domains match probability evaluation. They are validated
even when n is zero; valid empty requests return `[]`. Negative n/seed raises
1001, a request above one million raises 1007, and nonfinite distribution parameters
raise 1003. Scalar argument conversion/type failures follow the repository's
runtime-error convention (code zero) rather than StatsError categories.

A quantile that exceeds binary64 range raises 1003 and rejects the entire batch;
no partial results, dropped samples or replacement infinities are returned. Very
heavy tails/extreme scales can therefore fail even with finite parameters. Count
precision follows the existing discrete-quantile convention and binary64 limits.
The sampling limit bounds a single output allocation; callers retain control of
overall workload and parameter coordinates.

## Independent verification

`tests/generate-rng-fixtures.py` independently implements the ChaCha20 block
equations, PCG seed expansion and Open01 mapping. It never calls the extension or
rand. `tests/generate-rng-fixtures.R` maps those saved uniforms through base-R
quantiles. Python preserves full integer seeds and exact uniform bits while R
supplies the independent transformed reference values.

The saved `tests/fixtures/rng-python-r.json` contains **25 cases, 2,000 values**:
384 exact uniform values at four seeds (including zero and PHP_INT_MAX), all 13
families, three additional normal seed cases, and five point masses. Rust checks
all values; PHP checks the 1,616 transformed references. Uniform/discrete values
match exactly; continuous reference tolerance is `1e-15 + 1e-12*abs(reference)`.
Both suites check repeatability, prefixes, state isolation, domains/limits and
nonfinite samples. The uniform, categorical and permutation samplers are checked
against the documented maps applied to the fixture's Python uniforms. Deterministic normal/Poisson moment checks complement the
reference vectors. PHP additionally verifies parameter names/defaults and strict
seed/count types.

```sh
python3 tests/generate-rng-fixtures.py # Intentional Python/R reference refresh
python3 scripts/reference-manifest.py
cargo test -p stats-core --locked --test rng
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/rng.php
PHP=/path/to/matching/php PHP_CONFIG=/path/to/php-config ./scripts/check
```

The offline release gate needs neither Python RNG packages nor R for sampling
tests. Fixture provenance includes the Python and R generators, versions, seeds,
uniform inputs, expected quantities and hashes. The MIT license notices for the
new direct dependencies are retained under `third-party/`.
